newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece's Phoenix Credit Insurance aims high in 97.
newsitem.headline: Greece's Phoenix Credit Insurance aims high in 97.

text.p: Phoenix Credit Insurance SA, a subsidiary of state Commercial Bank and Phoenix General Insurance, aims to triple revenues in 1997 as it attempts to tap into credit insurance market.

Set up in 1995, the company will also bank on the know-how of its other shareholders, Europe's largest credit insurance operators -- France's Euler Group, formerly SFAC, and Germany's Hermes Kreditversicherungs AG.

"It is a great initiative for the Greek market. Phoenix Credit Insurance is well poised for growth helped by synergies within the Commercial Bank group," board chairman George Kotsalos told a press conference.
With a share capital of 900 million drachmas, the company aims to insure Greek business and industry against credit risk -- both foreign and domestic.

Every business which sells its products or services on credit must strive to secure its receivables. And growing international competition is forcing more and more business to be more lenient on their sales credit policies.
This entails potential dangers when clients default. Credit insurance is the best way to protect trade receivables.
Both group Euler and Hermes hold 17 percent stakes in Phoenix Credit Insurance along with Commercial Bank's five percent and Commercial Factoring's 10 percent.
Phoenix General Insurance is the majority shareholder with 51 percent.
In its first nine operating months, the company had revenues from insurance premiums of 200 million drachmas.
Its premiums are usually less than one percent of the insured value with a limit of $2.5 million drachmas of insurance coverage per transaction which may be raised to $4.0 million, executives said.
Paris-based Societe Francaise d'Assurances Credit (SFAC), recently renamed Euler, is 54 percent owned by the AGF Group and is the leading credit insurance company in France.
Hamburg-based Hermes is a subsidiary of Allianz AG which holds a majority 85 percent stake. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
